Container.Name: RDAPI
Container.Overview:
Lean self-hosted API server for the RustDesk app. Adds sign-in in the app, a personal address book that syncs to every device, a device list and a history of incoming connections to your own RustDesk ID and relay server, plus a web interface in six languages. Two-factor sign-in, passkeys, single sign-on (OpenID Connect) and daily backups. One container, one SQLite file.
On the first visit of the web interface you create the admin account; the setup code it asks for is printed to the container log. Then enter http://[server]:21114 (or your HTTPS address) as API server in the RustDesk app.
Public beta: the official RustDesk ID server up to 1.1.16 cannot connect a signed-in app yet. Until RustDesk releases the fix, sign out in the app before connecting.
Container.Requires: Your own RustDesk ID and relay server (hbbs/hbbr). For use over the internet, put RDAPI behind a reverse proxy with HTTPS.

Config.Name: Web interface and API
Config.Description: Port for the web interface and the API of the RustDesk app.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Database and daily backups. Must be writable for the user the container runs as (99:100, see Extra Parameters).

Config.Name: Default language
Config.Description: de, en, fr, es, it or nl. Empty: the browser language decides.

Config.Name: Secret key
Config.Description: Optional long random value (e.g. openssl rand -base64 48). Stores the two-factor keys encrypted. Keep it; without it, two-factor sign-in has to be set up again.

Config.Name: Daily backups to keep
Config.Description: Number of daily backups in /data/backups. 0 turns daily backups off.

Config.Name: History days
Config.Description: History and sign-in log are deleted after this many days.

Config.Name: Trusted reverse proxies
Config.Description: Addresses of reverse proxies whose X-Forwarded-For is trusted. Never use *.
